properties.description:
THE LESSON: a wildcard in a schema is not a permission, it is a silence, and silence gets written into data.

`REALIZES` is declared `to: "*"`. `link_artifact` ended in `self.realizes(...)` whatever the target was. So registering the file that IS a check — the exact step `quantity_check_without_executable_form` tells a reader to take — drew REALIZES onto a Verification, which the schema's own hint on IMPLEMENTS calls the wrong edge for that pair: "Not REALIZES (that says a file implements a CAPABILITY; a check interrogates one rather than providing it)." The note beside IMPLEMENTS had even predicted the failure mode in advance — "a wildcard would ACCEPT this pair and never MODEL it" — and the wildcard accepted it for months.

⭐ THE HALF THAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING: the fix did not add a single test. It corrected how 46 already-existing links were recorded, and 36 capabilities that had been sitting in a grandfathered claim-only baseline turned out to have had a runnable check the whole time. The tests were never missing. The EDGE recording them was. That is the same shape as the number this whole arc started from — the code at 85% coverage while the record said otherwise — arriving a second time, one layer down, and it is why "the record is wrong" should be a candidate before "the work was not done".

MEASURED, before and after, on this design's own export:
  · Verifications with an executable form: 30 -> 71
  · capabilities verified by a check something re-runs: 22 -> 58
  · checks with a registered file and NO form (the trap): 40 -> 0
  · the ratchet's grandfathered baseline: 220 -> 184, pruned the same day it was set

AND THE RATCHET HELD WHILE THIS HAPPENED: zero capabilities newly claimed a check nothing implements, which is the one thing the gate exists to refuse.
properties.name: The instructed route finally produces a runnable check, and 40 checks stop lying about themselves
